_comment: qa-approval-policy.json — what the QA bot may approve, and under which identity.
Read by scripts/qa-pr-approve.sh (guards) and scripts/qa-gh.sh (identity).
WHY JSON, when the other files in policies/ are YAML: node-8 has jq 1.7 and no
yq (verified 2026-07-27), and nothing in scripts/ parses YAML. The two YAML
policies here are consumed by deploy.sh and pr-validate.yml, not by the review
path. A policy the approval guards cannot parse would have to fail closed on
every PR, so this one is JSON.
WHY IT LIVES IN policies/: CODEOWNERS makes this directory @adk47-only and
hydra sets require_code_owner_reviews, so widening the bot's authority needs a
code-owner approval. NOTE that the bot posts as adk47, which IS the universal
code owner, so its approval does satisfy that gate today.
CHANGED 2026-08-03 (Nick, explicit): Guard 3b used to REFUSE any PR touching
these paths, which meant the bot could not approve the change that would let
it approve more. That self-reference is now GONE — sensitive_paths only
ALERTS. The team was spending review time it does not have, and the
instruction was that QA must surface issues and approve once they are
resolved rather than hand work back. The trade is explicit and known: a PR
that widens the bot's own authority can now be auto-approved, with a loud
alert as the only backstop.
If that turns out to be too much, the fix is to list the specific path under
sensitive_paths_blocking (which still refuses, exit 11) — NOT to restore a
blanket refusal, which is what made the bot unusable for this team.

_field_notes.identity.bot_logins: Every login the bot has ever reviewed under. A SET, not one value: GraphQL returns Bot{login:'muso-qa-bot'} while REST returns 'muso-qa-bot[bot]', and PRs in flight across the cutover (or a kill-switch rollback) carry threads filed by 'adk47'. Guard 8 matches membership; drop 'adk47' only once no open PR carries an adk47-filed REBASE WARNING thread.
_field_notes.identity.app_repos: Repos whose gh calls run as the App. Empty = every call falls through to the ambient host login, i.e. behaviour identical to before the shim existed. Grows one repo at a time during cutover.
_field_notes.merge_gate_repos: Repos where `qa-review` is a REQUIRED status check, i.e. GitHub holds the merge until the bot reports success. On these repos every dispatch path MUST end in a reported status: GitHub never times out a required check that was never reported, so a silently-skipped review makes the PR permanently unmergeable. scripts/qa-review-status.sh owns that lifecycle and .github/workflows/qa-autoreview.yml calls it on every exit path. The check must also be app-pinned (checks:[{context,app_id}]) or anyone with repo write could post a green qa-review and bypass the gate — which requires the App, not a user, to be what posts it.
_field_notes.merge_gate_repos_INTENTIONALLY_EMPTY: Muso-AI/hydra is the intended first (and for now only) entry, but this list stays EMPTY until two prerequisites land, because populating it starts seeding `pending` on real PRs: (1) the stale-pending watchdog that drives a lost dispatch to `failure` — it does NOT exist yet, and the comments in qa-autoreview.yml name it as the backstop; (2) the fix to scripts/qa-dispatch-pr-review.sh's stale sweep, which deletes never-run cron jobs and so can silently lose a review. Adding a repo here before those exist means a lost dispatch leaves a permanently pending gate with no automatic recovery.
_field_notes.author_deny: PR authors the bot must never approve. 'adk47' preserves today's behaviour exactly: GitHub's self-approval block used to make this impossible, and a dedicated identity would silently remove it. Flipping this to [] is a deliberate separate decision, not a side effect of the identity migration.
_field_notes.require_human_codeowner_repos: Repos where require_code_owner_reviews is on. This changes the bot's reporting ONLY where the repo is ALSO in identity.app_repos: a GitHub App can never be a CODEOWNER (CODEOWNERS takes users and teams only), so there the approval counts toward the required review but does NOT unblock merge. With app_repos empty (today) every call runs as the host account, which IS the universal code owner under hydra's CODEOWNERS — so the approval DOES clear the gate, verified on hydra#786 and #777 (both APPROVED, then mergeStateStatus CLEAN). The skill must relay the wrapper's post-check reviewDecision/mergeStateStatus rather than predict either outcome; asserting 'still needs a human CODEOWNER' when it does not was the friction removed on 2026-08-03.
_field_notes.sensitive_paths: Prefix-matched against the PR's changed files. A hit ALERTS and the approval proceeds (Notice 3b) — it stopped refusing on 2026-08-03; see the _comment block. The list must cover every input that defines the bot's own review authority, not just the executables: skills-all/muso-github-code-review/ is included because a PR editing the reviewer SKILL to skip the lens workflow, or to post qa-review=success directly, weakens the gate just as effectively as editing qa-pr-approve.sh. scripts/check-blast-radius.sh is included for the same reason — it defines what counts as high-impact. Since a hit no longer blocks, the ALERT is the entire protection: if the reviewing skill stops relaying it, these entries do nothing.
_field_notes.sensitive_paths_blocking: Same prefix matching, but a hit REFUSES (exit 11). Ships EMPTY: nothing blocks unless a path is deliberately opted back in after the 2026-08-03 change. This is the only surviving hard path gate, so the reader fails CLOSED — an unreadable or malformed key refuses rather than degrading to 'nothing blocks'.
_field_notes.advisory_checks: Per-repo, like every sibling list here. A check whose name STARTS WITH one of these is excluded from Guard 6's CI-green refusal and alerted on instead — for gates that test live server state rather than the diff (the deploy pre-flight rsync dry-run reds on pre-existing /opt/hydra drift). Matching is startswith, NOT contains: .github/workflows/ is only alert-guarded now, so a substring test would let a PR add a job whose name merely contains the token and buy itself an exemption. Entries must be real CHECK names (job names or status contexts) — a gate that is a STEP inside another job cannot be named here, because the rollup only ever shows the enclosing job (that job is 'validate', which must never be exempted).
